text:
Naked you demand the creatures, to dress them in you,
to cast these transparent, pure cloaks over their shoulders,
transforming flesh into soul;
snatching away the age-old dust of the soil,
washing them of furrow, fermented pollen,
the fruit-acid of harvests.

They are your jewels when you bathe them.
Purified of their seven black bulls, if you touch them.
Sparkling with almost human virtues
through your divine contact.

You corrode their bark,
dissolve their ripe, scaly tunics.
You save, like John’s baptism,
a whole genesis of sins.

Yes. Naked, your hoarse and delicate shell awaits us
to be born again in the sea that you are
into a peace of the spirit, set free.

Like microscopic lava we leave on your shore
the dirty sands of sorrowful sins.

translation.title: Naked You Demand Them, to Dress Them in You…
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The poem’s baptismal cleansing and geological imagery are retained.
